paragraphs: My name is May. I live in the white house next to the school. My brother Pat, my parents, and Grandma live there, too. Every morning, Grandma cooks rice soup for breakfast. The soup is hot and has a lovely smell. The smell wakes Pat at six o'clock. We eat together at half past six. Then we walk to school, and our class starts at eight o'clock. At twelve o'clock, we eat lunch in the canteen.

Today the morning is different. Pat does not wake up at six o'clock, because he was up late last night. At a quarter to eight, I say, "Pat, get up!" "We are late," I say. Pat puts on his uniform quickly, but he has no time for breakfast. Grandma gives him a piece of bread, but he says, "No, thank you." "Pat, are you sure?" asks Grandma. We run to school, and we arrive just before eight.

At ten o'clock, Pat comes to my room. His legs shake a little, and he feels weak. "I am thirsty, and I am hungry," he says. "Do you want some water?" I ask. I take him to the canteen. He drinks a big glass of water. Then he eats some rice with an egg. "This is lovely," says Pat. "But Grandma's soup is better."

After school, Grandma waits at the door of our house. She holds a warm cup of water with honey. "Drink this, Pat," she says. "Tomorrow, you must get up at six o'clock." Pat sits on the step and drinks the honey water slowly. He smiles, and his face is happy again. Tomorrow, we will eat breakfast together again.
text.summary: Every morning, May and Pat eat breakfast with their grandma before school. Today Pat is late and has no breakfast, so he feels weak and thirsty at school.
